h1: The 6 Best Vertical Mice for Mac Users of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Vertical Mice for Mac: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 vertical mice for Mac compared on Bluetooth, dongle needs, macOS software, button count and price bracket for wrist comfort.
summary: The Logitech MX Vertical is the best vertical mouse for Mac, with Bluetooth, a 2.4GHz option and companion macOS software for button mapping. The Logitech Lift is the better fit for small and average hands, the Razer Pro Click V2 adds six programmable buttons, and the ProtoArc EM11 NL is the budget pick that pairs over Bluetooth.
intro: Mac owners get caught by one detail when they buy a vertical mouse: the connector. A mouse that ships with a USB-A dongle and nothing else is a hassle on a laptop with only USB-C ports, and a model with no Bluetooth is not an option at all on some setups. The vertical shape grabs the headlines, but the connection method is what determines whether the mouse is pleasant on a MacBook or a daily annoyance.

This ranking covers six vertical mice that work with macOS, sorted by connectivity, software support and fit. We reviewed spec sheets and listings rather than running them on a desk, and we say clearly when a listing offers no dedicated macOS app. Button remapping, scroll behavior and gestures matter more on a Mac than raw sensor numbers, so those carry the most weight.

products.name: Logitech MX Vertical Wireless Mouse Ergonomic Design
products.verdict: The most complete Mac vertical mouse: Bluetooth, a dongle option, a rechargeable cell and real software.
products.description:
The MX Vertical connects over Bluetooth or a 2.4GHz receiver, charges its internal battery, and works with Logitech's companion macOS software for remapping buttons. It sits at the premium end of the vertical-mouse market, and the build reflects that.

It earns first place by solving the Mac-specific problems. Bluetooth means no dongle in a USB-C-only laptop, while the receiver is a fallback if the connection gets flaky. The companion app lets you assign buttons to gestures and shortcuts that match how macOS works, which matters because a vertical mouse changes how your hand reaches the buttons. Against the Lift below, it is larger and more expensive.

Buy it if you work on a Mac all day and want the most mature software. Skip it if your hands are small, since the body is large.
products.idealFor: Mac users who work all day and want the best software.
products.skipIf: You have small hands or a tight budget.

products.award: Best for Small to Medium Hands
products.name: Logitech Lift Vertical Ergonomic Wireless Mouse
products.verdict: The same software and Bluetooth, in a smaller body that fits average and small hands.
products.description:
The Lift is a compact vertical mouse with dual 2.4GHz and Bluetooth connectivity, a rechargeable battery and the Logitech companion macOS software. Pricing falls between $50 and $100.

Second place here is down to size and a slightly more modest feature set than the MX Vertical. For many Mac users the compact body is the better ergonomic choice, because a vertical mouse that is too big forces your fingers to stretch. A smaller footprint also travels well, and the price drop is meaningful. Compared with the budget picks below, it brings proven software and a more refined shell.

Choose it if your hand length is small to average and you want Logitech support behind the mouse. Skip it if you have large hands that need palm support.
products.idealFor: Mac users with small to average hands who want software support.
products.skipIf: Your hand needs a full-size vertical body.

products.name: Razer Pro Click V2 Vertical Wireless Mouse, 6 Button Ergonomic Design
products.verdict: Six programmable buttons and wireless connectivity for Mac users who live in shortcuts.
products.description:
The Pro Click V2 offers six programmable buttons, wireless connectivity and a rechargeable battery, in the $50 to $100 bracket. It is aimed at office workers who want more shortcuts under their thumb than a standard mouse provides.

It lands third because the listing does not make macOS software support as clear as Logitech's does, and the review base behind it is smaller. A button-heavy mouse is only as good as the tool that maps those buttons, so confirm macOS compatibility of the configuration software before you buy. When it works, six buttons are a genuine productivity gain for tasks like switching desktops.

It suits Mac users who want shortcut access within thumb reach. Skip it if you want proven macOS software out of the box.
products.idealFor: Mac power users who want many assignable buttons.
products.skipIf: You need mature macOS configuration software.

products.name: ProtoArc EM11 NL Wireless Ergonomic Vertical Mouse, Rechargeable
products.verdict: Bluetooth and a dongle in a rechargeable mouse for under $25, with no macOS app.
products.description:
The EM11 NL offers both Bluetooth and a wireless dongle, a built-in rechargeable battery and a budget price under $25. The listing notes no dedicated macOS companion app, so button remapping is limited to what the system provides.

It ranks fourth because Bluetooth is the right feature for a Mac and it is the cheapest model here to include it. It lacks the polish and software of the Logitech models, but for pointing, clicking and scrolling it does the core job. Compared with the Anker below, Bluetooth makes it much more flexible on modern laptops.

Choose it to trial the vertical shape without spending much, or as a travel mouse. Skip it if you want custom buttons.
products.idealFor: Mac users who want a cheap way to try a vertical mouse.
products.skipIf: You rely on remapped buttons and gestures.

products.name: Anker 2.4G Wireless Ergonomic Mouse, Right Hand Vertical Mouse
products.verdict: A right-hand-only, dongle-based mouse under $25 that needs a USB-C adapter on newer Macs.
products.description:
The Anker is a right-hand vertical mouse that connects through a 2.4GHz USB-A dongle. The listing mentions no dedicated macOS companion app, and the price is under $25.

It ranks fifth because a USB-A dongle is awkward on Macs that offer only USB-C ports, so a hub or adapter is probably part of the deal. The design is also right-hand specific, which excludes left-handed users. Against the ProtoArc, it gives up Bluetooth and a rechargeable battery on the listing, though a trusted accessory brand counts for something.

Buy it if you own a Mac with a USB-A port or already carry an adapter. Skip it if you want a clean wireless setup.
products.idealFor: Right-handed Mac users with a USB-A port or adapter.
products.skipIf: You are left-handed or use a USB-C-only laptop.

products.name: TECKNET Wired Mouse, Comfortable Ergonomic Mouse with 6400 DPI
products.verdict: A wired USB mouse with 6400 DPI that skips pairing entirely.
products.description:
The TECKNET is a wired USB ergonomic mouse with an adjustable sensor up to 6400 DPI, priced under $25. There is no battery to charge and no pairing, and the listing states no dedicated macOS companion app.

It ranks last because a cord undoes part of the freedom a vertical mouse offers, and a wired USB connector is a nuisance on laptops with only USB-C ports. On the other hand, it never runs out of charge and has no lag from interference. Compared with the Anker, it avoids the dongle that can get lost.

It makes sense for a fixed desktop Mac with a free USB port. Skip it for a MacBook you carry around.
products.idealFor: Desktop Mac setups with a spare USB port.
products.skipIf: You carry a MacBook between rooms.

whatMatters.detail: Many recent Macs have only USB-C ports, so a USB-A dongle needs an adapter and uses a port. Bluetooth pairs once and leaves every port free. Check the listing for the word Bluetooth, not just wireless, since wireless often means a dongle only.

Vertical mice move your thumb and fingers to unfamiliar positions, so remapping buttons can fix awkward reaches. Logitech offers companion macOS software, while several budget models list none. Without software, you are limited to system pointer and scroll settings.

A vertical mouse that is too large makes your fingers stretch, and one that is too small cramps the palm. Measure from wrist crease to middle fingertip, and compare with the maker's size note. Compact bodies like the Lift suit smaller hands, while the MX Vertical suits larger ones.

Most vertical mice are shaped for the right hand, and the Anker is explicitly right-hand specific. Left-handed users should look for a stated left-hand or ambidextrous model before buying. A mirrored shape is not a given in this category.

Rechargeable mice charge by cable and avoid replacing cells, which is convenient on a desk where a USB-C cable already lives. Wired models need none. Look for the words built-in rechargeable on a listing to make sure you are not buying a battery-hungry model.

faq.q: Will a vertical mouse work with my Mac without drivers?
faq.a: Yes, standard pointing and scrolling work without any installed software on macOS. Companion apps only add button remapping and gestures. Models without a macOS app still work as basic mice.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake Mac users make?
faq.a: Buying a dongle-only mouse for a USB-C laptop. You end up carrying an adapter, and the receiver is easy to lose. Choose Bluetooth where you can.

faq.q: Is the Logitech MX Vertical worth it over the Lift?
faq.a: If your hands are large and you want palm support, yes. For smaller hands the Lift is the better fit and costs less. Both offer the same style of Bluetooth and software support.

faq.q: How long does it take to adjust to a vertical grip?
faq.a: Plan on a week or two of everyday work. Your forearm sits in a handshake position, which feels strange at first, and pointer precision settles as the muscles adapt. Raise the tracking speed a notch while you adjust.

faq.q: Can I use these on multiple devices?
faq.a: The Logitech models list both Bluetooth and a receiver, so you can switch between a Mac and another computer. Check the listing for easy-switch buttons if you plan to share the mouse. Budget models generally pair with one device at a time.

faq.q: How do I clean a vertical mouse?
faq.a: Wipe the shell with a slightly damp cloth and a little isopropyl alcohol, and clear dust from the sensor window with a dry brush. Do this every few weeks, since skin oil builds up on the thumb rest.

finalTake: The Logitech MX Vertical is the best vertical mouse for a Mac if your hand is average or large, thanks to Bluetooth, a backup receiver and real macOS software. The Logitech Lift is the smarter choice for smaller hands, and the Razer Pro Click V2 earns a look if you want six programmable buttons. The ProtoArc EM11 NL is the budget answer, with Bluetooth for under $25. Avoid dongle-only models on a USB-C MacBook.
